title: Adaptive streaming load driver with network emulation and p95 regression alerting
creator: Avery Cho
description:
Build a scalable, adaptive load driver for streaming chat/completions (SSE + WebSocket) that simulates realistic user behavior, injects network conditions, measures tokens/sec and p95 end-to-end latencies, and automatically detects regressions. This driver should be able to run in CI (smoke), in dedicated scale labs for long-running regressions, and as part of nightly benchmarks.

Background: Existing runners hit limits when simulating long-lived streaming sessions with controlled KV-cache warmup, client-side backpressure, and churn. We need a single harness that can: 1) maintain thousands of concurrent streaming connections, 2) control each virtual client's token emission rate and prompt variety, 3) inject per-client network emulation (latency/jitter/packet loss), 4) emit metrics to Prometheus and an Influx-compatible store, and 5) support automated p95 regression detection with configurable baselines and alerting to Slack/ops.

Scope: Implement a Go-based driver (streambench) with pluggable SSE and WebSocket adapters, network emulation integration (tc/netem via a per-container sidecar), token-level accounting (tokens/sec and tokens/connection), p95 latency histograms by route/model, and a small queryable results exporter. Deliverables: harness code, CI job, a Grafana dashboard, and regression detection job that posts results to #perf-alerts and creates a Linear ticket when regression passes threshold.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can simulate 5k concurrent streaming clients on a single k8s node type used for scale lab (docs with resource profile)
Supports both SSE and WebSocket endpoints with identical scenario definition grammar
Per-client network emulation (latency/jitter/packet loss) configurable per scenario and applied via a sidecar; sample scenarios for 20ms/40ms/100ms RTT and 1% packet loss
Metrics exported: tokens/sec (global and per-model), p95 latency (end-to-end from first request byte to last event), connection churn rate, 5xx rate; metrics available in Prometheus/Grafana
Regression detection job: automatically compares nightly runs to baseline and opens a Linear ticket + notify #perf-alerts if tokens/sec drops >7% or p95 increases >15% for two consecutive runs
CI smoke job runs the harness with 50 clients and validates metric instrumentation and exporter health
Documentation: README with runbook, scenario format, example Grafana dashboard links, and costs/compute guidance
tasks: Design scenario DSL and client behavior model (prompt pools, token emission patterns, backpressure behavior)
Implement core Go harness with concurrent connection pool and SSE/WebSocket adapters
Add token accounting: token parser for streaming chunks and per-connection token counters
Integrate network emulation: container sidecar that applies tc netem rules per client pod
Instrument metrics: Prometheus exporter for tokens/sec, p95, error rates, connection lifecycle metrics
Create Grafana dashboard and predefined panels for automated job consumption
Implement regression detector: nightly job that fetches metrics, compares to baseline, computes drift, and posts to Slack + Linear
Wire up CI smoke job and internal runbook for running in scale lab
Load test run: execute three profile scenarios (low-latency, high-latency, lossy network) and record baseline
Clean up: docs, sample scenarios, and ownership handoff to SRE/perf owner
metrics: global_tokens_per_sec: gauge aggregated per-minute (derived from token counters)
p95_stream_latency_ms: 95th percentile of end-to-end streaming completion time
connection_setup_time_ms: time to establish SSE/WS connection
5xx_rate_percent: percentage of responses that returned 5xx errors
implementation_notes: Prefer Go for the harness: goroutines map well to long-lived streaming clients and we already have internal libraries for WS/SSE
Scenario DSL should be YAML and support weighted prompt pools and token pacing profiles (bursty vs steady)
Token accounting: implement a light-weight tokenizer that approximates our production tokenization for consistent tokens/sec numbers
Network emulation via tc requires privileged sidecar; for scale lab use a DaemonSet that runs a helper to apply per-pod qdisc rules
Exporter edgecases: ensure exporter survives transient collector outages and persists short-term aggregates to local disk for later reconciliation
CI integration: keep smoke run under 2 minutes by using 50 clients and validated synthetic prompts
Failure modes: be explicit about load-driver-induced overload vs platform regressions in the runbook
monitoring_plan: Nightly-run job (k8s CronJob) performs 30m run across three scenarios and stores raw metrics in perf-bench-archive
Regression detector checks last N=3 nightly runs; requires 2 consecutive failing deltas to avoid flapping
Alert thresholds: tokens/sec drop >7% (critical), p95 increase >15% (critical), 5xx rate >1% (warning)
On regression: post summary to #perf-alerts with run diffs and attach grafana snapshot; create Linear ticket with label perf-regression
On CI-failure: abort PR merge and annotate PR with harness output link and failing metric snapshot
